_metadata.description: Complete catalog of all projection assumptions in the DecarbIQ pipeline
_metadata.notes: None of these variable projections have documented external sources or uncertainty ranges. All are hardcoded trends in step6 (MC) and step11 (projection map). Assumptions are duplicated in both steps to ensure consistency.

CAP.description: Hard ceiling on gas price — reflecting floor in log-space
CAP.source: Hardcoded (historical max monthly avg was ~$9 in 2022, $15.39 in 2005)

FLOOR.description: Production cost floor — reflecting floor in log-space
FLOOR.source: Lowest monthly avg HH in 29 years = $1.49 (Mar 2024)

START.description: Pulled from master dataset at runtime, not hardcoded

mean_reversion.description: Schwartz (1997) one-factor model: d(ln P) = κ(ln θ − ln P)dt + σ dW

speed_normal.actual: Data-estimated from AR(1) on log-prices, normal months (line 5998-6011)
speed_normal.description: Monthly mean-reversion speed κ. AR(1): log(P_t) = c + φ × log(P_{t-1}) + ε; κ = -ln(φ)
speed_normal.source: Fallback hardcoded; actual estimated from data

speed_crisis.actual: Data-estimated from AR(1) on ALL transitions involving crisis months (entry + within + exit), not just crisis-crisis pairs
speed_crisis.description: Higher speed = faster reversion from extreme levels during crises. Enforced minimum: 1.5× speed_normal (physical constraint: crises are temporary)
speed_crisis.methodology_change: v2: expanded AR(1) sample from crisis-crisis pairs only to all pairs where at least one month is crisis. Captures entry/exit dynamics. Added floor at 1.5× normal speed.
speed_crisis.source: Data-driven with physical constraint (crisis events have bounded duration)

garch_era_structure.description: 3-era GARCH estimation with materiality test (step3, lines 5276-5389)

pre_shale.description: Tight supply, weather-driven spikes, high vol (~52%)

post_shale.description: Abundant shale gas supply, lower vol (~46%)

post_covid.description: LNG exports, geopolitical shocks, intermediate vol (~66%)

selection_logic.materiality_test: If |post_shale_vol - post_covid_vol| > 15% OR |persistence_diff| > 0.03 → eras are materially different → use post_covid

gas_regime_classification.rule: If any active event has type in (hurricane, polar_vortex, geopolitical) AND |gas_price_impact| >= 1.5 → ng_crisis; else → normal
gas_regime_classification.threshold_source: Derived from disruptions catalog — events below 1.5 are minor

crisis_level_shift_hh.value: Data-estimated from H2 interaction model is_ng_crisis coefficient

crisis_garch.method: Constant variance (empirical) because n≈38 < 50 threshold for GARCH convergence

event_model.description: Multi-month event draws in MC simulation loop (step6, lines 6205-6323)
event_model.general_notes: Frequencies from 29-year named event catalog. Duration = persistence × magnitude. Linear decay over duration.

geopolitical.frequency: 0.034/yr (1 event in 29 years — only Russia-Ukraine 2022 qualified)
geopolitical.scaling: Scaled by geopolitical_model p_disruption / 0.50 (2024 baseline), clamped [0.5, 2.0]

renewable_overbuild.source: Empirical base + hardcoded growth rate assumption

expected_monthly_impulse.source: Computed from empirical frequencies × magnitudes × durations

policy_risk_model.description: Policy event probabilities for MC overlay (step4, lines 5648-5681)

ira_rollback_probability.election_proximity: 1.0 in even years (election), 0.5 in odd years

ira_rollback_gas_impact.description: Impact if IRA rolls back: no ITC/PTC → less renewable buildout → more gas dependence

queue_delay_probability.source: Hardcoded judgment based on queue growth trend

nem_reform_states.description: Number of states following CA NEM 3.0 model

variable_projections_step11.description: All hardcoded trend formulas for 21+ variables projected 2025-2035 (step11, lines 7337-7414). Duplicated in step6 projected_vars (lines 5860-5895) for MC targets.

us_data_center_twh.source: No source cited. CAGR appears to reference EIA/McKinsey estimates.

tx_data_center_twh.conversion: 1 GW data center ≈ 7.45 TWh/yr at 85% capacity factor
tx_data_center_twh.source: CNBC/ERCOT: 20-30 GW realistic by 2030, 78 GW ERCOT high forecast

electric_power_bcfd.description: Gas demand for electric power, slow growth with electrification

tx_demand_twh.formula: Compound growth: 14% declining by 1%/yr to 7% floor
tx_demand_twh.source: ERCOT/CNBC: 7-14% annual demand growth driven by data centers, electrification, industrial expansion

lng_utilization_pct.description: LNG export facility utilization grows as capacity fills
lng_utilization_pct.source: No source cited. Hardcoded growth rate and cap.

us_ng_storage_vs_5yr_pct.description: Assumes normal storage levels (no deviation from 5-year avg)

itc_rate_pct.source: IRA legislation (known schedule through 2032); post-2032 phasedown is assumption

ptc_rate_cents_kwh.source: IRA legislation (known schedule through 2032); post-2032 phasedown is assumption

queue_backlog_gw.description: Peaks ~3000 GW by 2027 then slowly declines with FERC reforms

cumulative_ferc_reforms.description: Number of FERC reform actions, +1 per year, cap at 22

ira_active.source: Assumption: IRA stays active in base case

ca_battery_capacity_gw.source: No source cited. Hardcoded growth rate.

tx_battery_capacity_gw.formula: Piecewise: 13.9 GW through 2026, +11 GW/yr to 2029, +5 GW/yr after
tx_battery_capacity_gw.source: Modo Energy: 13.9 GW operational Jan 2026, 40-55 GW projected by 2029

ercot_congestion_avg.description: Rises with renewable growth and load growth

ercot_spike_count.description: Expected to moderate with battery storage growth

all_hdd_cdd.method: Constant — use historical average for all projection years

us_hdd_departure_pct.description: Assumes normal weather (no departure from average)

us_cdd_departure_pct.description: Assumes normal weather (no departure from average)

basis_model_citygate.description: California citygate gas price = HH + basis. Basis modeled by OLS (step6, lines 6063-6116)
basis_model_citygate.noise_method: Bootstrap from actual OLS residuals (NOT fitted normal — captures fat right tail to $25+)
basis_model_citygate.fallback: If model fails: constant basis = recent 24-month mean

variable_delta_caps.description: Each variable's delta (projection minus latest) is capped at ±2σ of in-sample range to prevent extrapolation (lines 5900-5910, 7472-7479)
variable_delta_caps.rationale: Regression coefficients only valid within observed variation range

scarcity_model_ercot.description: Log-log scaling model for electricity scarcity pricing (Variant H3, used in step11)
scarcity_model_ercot.normalization_rationale: ERCOT reduced VOLL cap from $9,000 to $5,000 in June 2022 — raw values not comparable

key_concerns: No external source citations for most variable projection slopes (GDP, gen mix, LNG)
No uncertainty ranges on any projection trend
CA battery +5 GW/yr appears aggressive vs literature (EIA/BNEF: +2.5-3 GW/yr)
TX data center quadratic growth assumes massive buildout — 25 GW by 2030, 78 GW by 2035 (ERCOT high forecast). If queue delays or permitting slow builds, actual could be much lower
TX demand 7-14% growth is historically unprecedented for a major grid — assumes sustained data center + industrial expansion
TX battery 11 GW/yr buildout (Modo Energy) is 3-4× current annual US battery additions — supply chain and permitting risks
LNG utilization linear growth to 92% may be optimistic given permitting headwinds
Weather is assumed 'normal' every year — no climate trend in CDD/HDD
Uri-type extreme (1-in-100-yr) probability is hardcoded judgment, not actuarially derived
Post-2032 ITC/PTC phasedown schedule is speculative
IRA rollback probability formula is subjective (no polling/legislative model basis)
TX data center TWh may exceed TX total demand TWh at high end — consistency check needed
